ISO 8434-1 is the international standard for 24° compression tube fittings, the cutting-ring type used with DIN 2353 light (L) and heavy (S) series. No test certificate is attached to the listing; tell us the documents your inspection or project needs when you ask for a quotation.

faqs.q: What does the Union Elbow Metric connect to?
faqs.a: On the Union Elbow Metric, port A is male DIN 24° cone L-series and S-series (M10×1 to M42×2) and port B is male DIN 24° cone L-series and S-series (M10×1 to M42×2). Each end mates with a part of the same thread and the same seat. The [DIN 2353 Bite Type Adapters](/c/din-2353-bite-type-adapters-uae) range lists the matching parts.

faqs.q: How do I fit the Union Elbow Metric so it does not leak?
faqs.a: Match the thread and the seat before you tighten the Union Elbow Metric. On a 24° cone end the tube goes through the nut and cutting ring and is pre-set into the cone, so cut the tube square, deburr it and preset the ring before final assembly. Clean the port first and never force a joint that does not start by hand. See our [guide to fitting make-up torque](/blog/hydraulic-fitting-make-up-torque) for more.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Union Elbow Metric and the Bulkhead Elbow Union Metric?
faqs.a: The Union Elbow Metric and the [Bulkhead Elbow Union Metric](/p/bulkhead-elbow-union-metric) are separate listings with their own size tables. The second adds bulkhead to the name. Choose by the thread and seat at each port you are connecting, not by the name, because adapters with similar names can have different ends.
